Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.gov.ph 5iLC ODIN\ON 31 S. 2021 Bia 06 HON. JAYVEE TYRON L. UY Vice Governor Office of the Vice Governor Province of Davao De Oro Dear Hon. Uy: This has reference to your letter dated December 7, 2022 to this Department requesting for guidance and legal opinion on the following matters: (1) On the Matter of Job-Order/Contract of Service Workers and (2) On the matter of Legislative Budget. We will be discussing the two subject matters separately. (I) On the matter of Job-Order/Contract of Service Workers On July 1, 2022, One Hundred (100) Job Order (JO) contracts were contracted by the Office of the Vice Governor and assigned at the Vice Governor's Office, Sangguniang Panlalawigan, and offices of the Provincial Board Members, respectively. The JO contracts were based on available funds for the CY 2022 under the Provincial Legislative Department which is provided under the Appropriation Ordinance of the Province for year 2022. These were subsequently renewed and effective for a period of three (3) months until the PHRMDO's letter instructing the non-processing of the salaries of JO employees for the Vice Governor, Sangguniang Panlalawigan and Provincial Board Members pursuant to DILG Opinion No. 43, series of 2022. On the other hand, the Office of the Governor did not revoke, cancel or terminate the aforementioned JO contracts, but remained steadfast with the PHRMDO's stand pursuant to this Department's legal opinion. In view of the foregoing, the following points of clarification are herein raised: (a) The case Atienza vs. Villarosa supersedence over the case of Vicencio vs. Villarl; the two types of Job Order employees and the persons who are authorized to appoint them as indicated in DILG Opinion No. 31 , series of 2019, DILG Opinion No. 34, series of 2014 and DILG Opinion No. 89, series of 2022 still applicable; (b) What is the status of the job order contracts entered in good faith by the Vice- Governor? (c) Since the contract was not terminated or cancelled by the Governor, is the contract still binding such that the JO workers are entitled to pay for services rendered? "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54



(d) In case the Governor will not pay the JO workers, what remedies are available for the Vice Governor on one hand and for the JO worker on the other? (e) Will the deliberate refusal of the Governor to respect the contracts entered into by the Vice-Governor for the benefit of the Provincial government constitute undue interference and abuse of authority considering these contracts are beneficial to the Province? (f) Whether or not the appropriation for Job Order/Contract of Service in the Legislative Department operates as an express authorization for the Vice Governor to hire JO workers in the Legislative Department and sign respective contracts? Anent the first query, we would like to put into light DILG Legal Opinion No. 34, S. 2014 which sufficiently discussed and clarified the following points of clarification raised in the question particularly on the two types of job order employees and the persons authorized to appoint them. It is important to emphasize that the case of Atienza vs. Villarosa, clearly delineated the authority of the Governor as against the Vice-governor's hiring authority as it is the budget source of the salaries which sets the employees and officials of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan apart from other employees and officials of the province. In addition, the pronouncements of the Supreme Court in the case of Vicencio vs. Villarl did not supersede the Atienza case but instead provided an exception rather than the general rule. Under this provision, therefore, there is no inherent authority on the part of the city vice-mayor to enter into contracts on behalf of the local government unit, unlike that provided for the city mayor. Thus, the authority of the vice-mayor to enter into contracts on behalf of the city was strictly circumscribed by the ordinance granting it. Ordinance No. 15-2003 specifically authorized Vice-Mayor Yambao to enter into contracts for consultancy services. As this is not a power or duty given under the law to the Office of the Vice-Mayor, Ordinance No. 15-2003 cannot be construed as a "continuing authority" for any person who enters the Office of the Vice-Mayor to enter into subsequent, albeit similar, contracts. Applying the foregoing to the instant case, it is clear that the casual employees in the Sangguniang Panlalawigan and of the Office of the Vice-Governor which fall under those not provided for in the plantilla and hired through JO regardless of source of funds are authorized to be hired by the Governor based on Sec. 77, Sec. 465 (b)(i)(v) of the Local Government Code. For the succeeding questions, we will be discussing these together. We refer the matter to DILG Opinion No. 43 s. 2022, which ruled in the affirmative as to whether an Appropriation Ordinance authorizing the Annual Budget of the City is enough to support as basis for authority to hire individuals as job order/contract of service. We quote in verbatim. We, therefore, reiterate the modification effected by DILG Opinion No. 34 s. 2014 which state as follows: "In view of the recent ruling of the Supreme Court in the [sic] Villar case, the Department's opinion as embodied in DILG Opinion No. 23-2005, 17-2010, and 2011 are hereby modified. As a general rule, all contracts G.R. No. 182069. JWy03, 2012 Page 2 of 4

of services and job orders shall be entered into by the local chief executive of the local government unit, except in cases where there is an ordinance passed by the sanggunian specifically authorizing the vice-mayor or vice-governor to enter into contracts on behalf of the local government unit." For the third query, we submit an affirmative view as to the budgetary aspect relative to the hiring. [emphasis supplied] It is to be reminded, however, that other bases may be required by other pertinent laws relative tc accounting and auditing regulations. Applying the foregoing to the instant case, the existence of the Province's Appropriation Ordinance for the year 2022 showed that there was in fact available funds for the salary of the JO contracts hired by the Provincial Legislative Department. Hence, the Annual Budget of the Province is sufficient basis for the authority to hire individuals as job order/contract of service. As to the other matters raised herein relative to JO contracts, pursuant to this Department's Memorandum Order No. 2010-022, this Department respectfully declines to provide its input as the questions raised are justiciable in nature and are best resolved in the proper forum. (2) On the matter of legislative budget: In October 2022, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, through the Office of the Vice Governor, submitted its proposed budget for the operations of the Legislative Department for 2023 to the Office of the Governor. Among the items included is the allocation for the JO workers in the amount of Php 8,370,000.00 under the item on MOOE - Other Services for the legislative department. Thereafter, the 2023 Executive Budget Proposal was submitted to the Office of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan for the enactment of the Appropriation Ordinance. According to your representations, after October 16, 2022, the Office cf the Governor submitted an amendment to the proposed executive budget, omitting the allocation for JO Personnel in the legislative department in its entirety. The Office of the Vice Governor maintained that the hiring of the JO workers is necessary and crucial with the demands of the service and processes in the ISO Standardization. Hence, the following queries: (a) May the Governor unilaterally diminish or omit an item in the proposed budget submitted by Legislative Department? (b) What remedies would be available for the Legislative Department to insist on its appropriation? (c) May the Sangguniang Panlalawigan disregard the amended executive budget for having been filed beyond October 16, 2022 and consider only the proposed executive budget that was timely submitted? Otherwise stated, may the Governor still amend the submitted proposed executive budget after October 16, 2022. 2 RE: Supplement to Memorandum Order No. 2010-01 dated March 4, 2010; par (1) those containing facts that are justiciable in nature. Justiciable issues are those that require adjudication by the courts cf law as to who between the opposing parties have the better right over a given controversy. Page 3 of 4

Anent the first and second questions, Article 415(b) of the implementing rules and regulations of the LGC is enlightening, thus: Veto Power of the Local Chief Executive — The local chief executive may veto any ordinance of the sangguniang panlalawigan, sangguniang panlungsod, or sangguniang bayan on the ground that it is ultra vires or prejudicial to the public welfare, stating his reasons therefore in writing. The local chief executive, except the punong barangay, shall exercise the power to veto any particular item or items of an appropriations ordinance, or an ordinance or resolution adopting a local development plan and public investment program, or an ordinance directing the payment of money or creating liability. In such cases, the veto shall not affect the item or items which are not objected to. The vetoed item or items shall not take effect unless the sanggunian overrides the veto in the manner provided in Rule XVII of these Rules; otherwise, the item or items in the appropriations ordinance of the previous year corresponding to those vetoed, if any, shall be deemed reenacted. As to the last query, Sec. 318 is controlling, to wit: SECTION 318. Preparation of the Budget by the Local Chief Executive. - Upon receipt of the statements of income and expenditures from the treasurer, the budget proposals of the heads of departments and offices, and the estimates of income and budgetary ceilings from the local finance committee, the local chief executive shall prepare the executive budget for the ensuing fiscal year in accordance with the provisions of this Title. The local chief executive shall submit the said executive budget to the Sanggunian concerned not later than the sixteenth (16th) of October of the current fiscal year. Failure to submit such budget on the date prescribed herein shall subject the local chief executive to such criminal and administrative penalties as provided for under this Code and other applicable laws. [emphasis supplied] A close scrutiny of the cited provisions above expressly provides that it is within the ambit of the local chief executive to veto any ordinance of the sangguniang panglalawigan, panlungsod or bayan in case the latter is found to be ultra vires or prejudicial to the public welfare. However, considering that the local chief executive or the governor in this case, failed to act not later than the period required by law or the sixteenth (16) of October, the budget appropriation timely filed by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan cannot be subjected to further amendments by the Office of Governor. This opinion is without prejudice to any contrary opinion, decisions, and orders of competent authorities or courts. We hope to have assisted you on this matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY ATTY.
